name: rule ordering and tie-breaks
description:
Pins the resolution order when more than one rule matches. A deliberately small policy: every rule here matches every request, so the only thing under test is which one wins.

This vector exists because the tie-break is the part of the engine that fails silently. If `deny` stopped outranking `allow` at equal priority, every functional test would still pass and the system would fail open — which is the wrong direction for a component whose entire purpose is constraint.

rules.description: Matches only artifact_write, priority 1 — outranks all of the above by number.

cases.name: deny outranks require_approval and allow at equal priority
all three equal-priority rules are recorded as considered, strictest first
cases.description: The winner is not the only thing kept. A rule that fires constantly but never wins is a vacuous rule, and ADR-014 wants it visible.

cases.name: a lower priority number beats a stricter effect
cases.description: Priority is the primary key and severity only breaks ties. An explicit high-rank allow is how an exception to a broad deny is expressed, so this must not be inverted either.
